rows.author: B040
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 177 OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 209, KNOWN AS THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Since laws are created to serve the welfare of man and not otherwise, and since there is growing awarenes that there is no such thing as superior, laws should make an exemption to the general rule least we undermine and oppress the minorities of our society, like the "indigenous cultural communities", by forcing them to embrace the Family Code without due reference and consideration of their distinct culture. > Seeks, therefore, to AMEND Article 177 of EO No. 209 to read as follows:"Article 177.[Only] Children conceived and born outside of wedlock of parents who, at the time of the conception of the former were not disqualified by any impediment to marry each other, EXCEPT ON THE GROUND THAT EITHER OR BOTH THE PARENTS WERE BELOOW EIGHTEEN YEARS OF AGE, CAN [may] be legitimated. > LEGITIMATION ATTACHES TO CHILDREN WHOSE PARENTS WERE BELOW EIGHTEEN YEARS OF AGE AT THE TIME OF THEIR CONCEPTION OR BIRTH EVEN IN CASE EITHER OR BOTH PARENTS CONTRACTED THE MARRIAGE AFTER THE TERM
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 1997-08-20

rows.author: B048
rows.title_full: AN ACT BANNING STUDENTS IN THE PRIMARY AND SECONDARY SCHOOLS FROM ENTERING MALLS AND GAME SHOPS DURING SCHOOL DAYS
rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill intends to motivate and encourage students to devote their time for studies rather than visiting malls only for fun.  This calls for a joint effort between the State and the parents in their pursuit to provide quality educationby not tolerating students to go somewhere else after attending or during classes. > Declares the following UNLAWFUL: (1) Students in the primary and secondary schools entering shopping malls for video game shops; and (2) Establishments allowing theentry of students during school days. Provides penalties for violation of this Act.
rows.status: Approved on Second Reading on 1997-10-29

rows.author: B045
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE SLOPING AGRICULTURAL LAND TECHNOLOGY FARMING PROGRAM, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: To this end, the establishment of programs and farming techniques shall be undertaken to enhance income distribution in rural areas and help the rural poor in pursuing national self-sufficienc y in food production, particularly the hillside farmers.  This program shall not only improve the quality of their lives through greater production but shall also be designed to restore and conserve the fertility of the soil. > "SALT (Sloping Agricultural Land Technology) Farming Program" > Covers all public and private lands, including ancestral lands devoted to agriculture with a slope of at least five (5) degrees or higher, regardless of the agricultural products raised or can be raised thereon. Provides INCENTIVES to farmers applying tthe SALT farming method.
rows.status: Substituted by HB10514

rows.author: A101
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR EXTRAORDINARY PENALTIES FOR POSSESSION OF ILLEGAL DRUGS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Anti-Drug Possession Act" Declares the following --- " SECTION 2.  PRIMA FACIE EVIDENCE. The mere possession of prohibited drugs including but not limited to shabu, marijuana, cocaine and the like shall be prima facie evidence that the possessor isa user of prohibited drugs." Provides, likewise, for the following penalties: "SECTION 3. The penalty for possession of prohibited drugs shall be SIX YEARS  AND ONE DAY imprisonment and fine of P60,000.00 or both upon the discretion of the judge.  In the alternative, the accused may be required to render community service for the same period and/or be made to use clothing with proper markings "I AM A USER OF PROHIBITED DRUGS" or words to the effect. Furthermore, the State us ehreby allowed to ppaint markings of the same nature in the last known residence of the accused for the same period of time he was sentenced."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 1997-08-20

rows.title_full: AN ACT LEVELLING THE PLAYING FIELD IN THE OIL INDUSTRY BY REMOVING THE TARIFF DIFFERENTIAL BETWEEN IMPORTED CRUDE OIL AND IMPORTED REFINED PETROLEUM PRODUCTS BY AMENDING SECTION 5, PARAGRAPH (b) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8180, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: As we now experience, this difference in tariff rates betwen imported crude oil and imported refined petroleum products, unwittingly provided a built-in-advant age for the three existing oil refineries in the country and eliminating competition which is  a must in a free enterprise economy. Moreover, it created a disincentive for other players to engage even initially in the importation and distribution of refined petroleum products and ultimately in the putting up of refineries. This tariff differential virtually created a monopoly of the downstream oil industry by the existing three oil companies as shown by their uniform and capricious pricing of their products since this law took effect, to the great disadvantage of the conssuming public.> Thus, instead of achieving  the desired effects of deregulation, that of free enterprise and a level playing field in the downstream oil industry, RA 8180 has created an environment conducive to cartelization, unfavorable, increased,

rows.author: A005
rows.title_full: AN ACT WAIVING PENALTY INTEREST AND OTHER SIMILAR CHARGES ON AGRICULTURAL LOANS EXTENDED BY THE DEVELOPMENT BANK OF THE PHILIPPINES (DBP) TO BORROWERS RESIDING IN PLACES DECLARED AS CALAMITY AREAS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 81, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS "THE 1986 REVISED CHARTER OF THE DEVELOPMENT BANK OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill wants to make an exception: That in cases of calamities such as typhoons, floods, earthquakes, and others, penalty interest and other similar charges should be waived by the DBP. It is, likewise, a fact that after these calamities, borrowers have a hard time meeting their financial obligations. These financial obligations continue to accumulate once they default in the payment thereof because of penalty interest and other similar charges. Eventually, the failure to settle these financial obligations results in foreclosure. Thus, borrowers of agricultural loans, particularly farmers or farmers' cooperatives end up losing ownership of properties they used as collaterals or securities for the purpose.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 1997-08-20

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZ ING PSYCHOLOGICAL TESTING OF ELEMENTARY AND HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS TO DETERMINE THE FIELD OF STUDY MOST SUITED FOR FILIPINO STUDENTS, PROVIDING FOR COUNSELLING CENTERS IN EVERY SCHOOL DISTRICT, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill seeks to institutionaliz e a psychological testing scheme that shall help Filipino students determine the fields of study most suited to their talents and skills. "Psychological Test for Students Act" Mandates ALL students in public and private elementary and high schools to undergo psychological testing for the purpose of determining the field of study most suited for them.  >The tests shall consist of verbal and nonverbal tests.

rows.abstract: Rationale: One of the indicators of a progressive economy is the tremendous increase in the number  of construction projects. Most of these projects are undertaken by private contractors contracted by the government. However, it has been observed that many public works projects being undertaken by private contractors are substandard. rows.author: B009
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 30 (h) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6975, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE DILG ACT OF 1990, BY REDUCING THE HEIGHT REQUIREMENT TO QUALIFY FOR APPOINTMENT AS OFFICER OR MEMBER OF THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE (PNP)
rows.abstract: Rationale: The height requirement provided for under Republic Act No. 6975 for acceptance and appointment to the PNP, has long been the cause of unjust exclusion from the PNP and consequently has caused frustration of otherwise fully qualified indigenous Cordilleran applicants to the PNP , msot of whom are by nature and physical build, short and stocky. Since majority of the Cordillerans fall below the minimum height requirements provided for under Republic Act No. 6975, said law can be regarded as discriminatory towards Cordillerans and therefore unconstitutiona l since it has the effect of discriminating against a class of Filipino citizens. > Proposes, therefore, the following amendments to Section 30 of the DILG Act, RA 6975 on the genneral qualifications for appointment to the PNP: "Must be at least one meter and [sixty-two] FIFTY-SEVEN centimeters (1.57 m) in height for male and one meter and fifty-seven FIFTY-TWO centimers (1.52 m) for female.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SECURITY since 1997-08-26

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 30-H OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6975, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE DEPARTMENT OF INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT (DILG) ACT OF 1990
rows.abstract: Rationale: Experience and observations have shown that littel men can do or can even surpass what bigger men can do in the police or military service. Police and military veterans can attest to the outstanding achievements of little men in war and in the fight against lawless elements. What counts is the physcial and mental fitness of the policemen  or soldier and not his height. > Proposes the following amendment to Section 30 - h of RA 6975, the DILG Act: "SEC. 30 - h. Must be at least one meter and sixty-two centimeters (1.62 m.) in height for male and one meter and fifty-seven centimeters for female. EXEMPTION IS, HOWEVER, GIVEN TO MEMBERS OF THE CULTURAL COMMUNITIES WHO MUST BE AT LEAST ONE METER AND FIFTY-SEVEN CENTIMETERS (1.57 M.)FOR MALE AND ONE METER AND FIFTY-TWO (1.52 M.) FOR FEMALE."

rows.abstract: "Wage Policy Reform Act of 1997" Declares it the policy of the State to provide for and ensure  a living wage for the Filipino worker and improve the quality of his life. Mandates the following --- "SEC. 3. Operationalizin g  the Living Wage. - Uponthe effectivity of this Act, every covered employer shall pay to each of his employees a daily minimum wage equivalent to the mandated living  wage as computed by the Department of Labor and Employment, in coordination with  the National Census andStatistics Office, and genuine representatives of labor and management." Provides, likewise, for the grant of EMERGENCY LIVING ALLOWANCE.

rows.abstract: Rationale: The earning potential of footwear production has long been proven.  In 1996, the footwear industry earned US$170,043,570. 00. On the first half of 1997, it has already gained as much as US$94,347,096.0 0. This is 1.05% growth compared tothe industry's export earnings during the same period last year. rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A COCONUT SEEDLING NURSERY IN EVERY COCONUT-PRODUCI NG BARANGAY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The coconut industry needs to replace senile coconut trees planted in some one million hectares by the year 2000 in order to maintain, if not improve, its competitive position worldwide  and to enhance the productivity and incomes of some20 million Filipinos dependent on the industry. > The most basic  need for the attainment of this goal is good quality seednuts/seedli ngs. Mandates the following --- "SECTION 1. There shall be established in every coconut-produci ng  barangay a coconut seedling nursery, which shall be owned and/or maintained preferably by a  coconut small farmers organization oeprating in the barangay. The Philippine Coconut Authority, in coordination with local government units and farmers' organizations conccerned, shall pool their resources for the attainment of the objectives of this Act."

rows.abstract: Rationale: The measure provides for the acquisition and distribution through the Philippine Coconut Authority of moisture meters in all coconut-produci ng barangays in the country. > At present, Republic Act No. 1365 requires the use of moisture meters in all domestic purchases of copra for the purpose of ensuring good quality copra and better incomes for our coconut farmers. >Mandates the following --- "SECTION 1. Tne Philippine Coconut Authority shall formulate and implement a program for theacquisition of moisture meters and their distribution in every coconut-produci ng barangay, preferably through a duly accredited coconut small farmers' organization."

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE SCIENCE HERITAGE CENTER, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS FOR THE PURPOSE
rows.abstract: Provides for the creation of the PHILIPPINE SCIENCE HERITAGE CENTER which shall "highlight the country's contributions to the world of science and elicit a sense of pride in evey Filipino who learns of these accomplishments ." The Center shall --- (1) Document the work of Filipino scientists, ideas, inventions, and products which have had a significant impact on the improvement of human lives; (2) Establish a display area for samples of inventions and products, memorabilia, and references (library); (3) Produce printed materials to be used by schools in teaching values education with scientific insights. These materials will also serve as an alternative source of information for people unable to visit the Center; and (4) Serve as the coreof the network of science museums in the Philippines.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY since 1997-08-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING A TEN-YEAR MORATORIUM ON THE GATHERING OF EDIBLE BIRDS' NEST, PROVIDING A PENALTY THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Declares a MORATORIUM for a period of ten (10) years on the gathering, taking, collecting and destroying of the nests or "Collocalia Troglodytes" or swiflets. PROHIBITS, likewise, all catching, hunting, injuring, taking, possessing and/or killing ofsaid swiflets, as well as the act of driving them away from their natural habitats. Penalizes the violation of this proposed measure.

rows.author: A051
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED TWELVE HUNDRERD NINETEEN, AS AMENDED, ENTITLED 'PROVIDING FOR THE EXPLORATION, EXPLOITATION, UTILIZATION AND CONSERVATION OF CORAL RESOURCES'
rows.abstract: Rationale: It is a fact that dead corals are used for rip-rap purposes and/or for the construction of breakwaters to serve as a protection for seacrafts or vessels moored along the shorelines. The beneficial use of dead corals for these purposes should not, therefore, be prohibited nor penalized. There are over zealous BFAR people, however, who are prosecuting persons who have used dead corals for rip-rap and/or for the construction of breakwaters. Seeks to AMEND Section 5 of PD 1219 to read asfollows: "SEC. 5. Ordinary Coral. - The gathering, harvesting, collecting, transporting, [possession], sale and/or exporting of ordinary corals either in raw or processed form in any quantity, is prohibited. [The use of corals as materials in buildiing and other man-made structures, such as but not limited to piers, dams and dikes, is likewise prohibited.]"
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 1997-08-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT RATIONALIZING THE ORGANIZATION AND FUNCTIONS OF GOVERNMENT AGENCIES RELATED TO WATER, ABOLISHING THE NATIONAL WATER RESOURCES BOARD, CREATING THE WATER RESOURCES AUTHORITY OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The State recognizes the existence of a national water crisis. It is hereby declared the policy of the State to adopt urgent and effective measures to address the national water crisis, as well as measures for the long-term sustainable management of scarce water resources.  To achieve this purpose, the utilization and development of water resources must be rationalized and optimized through an integrated approach to planning, development and regulation of the water sector. "The WaterResources Authority of the Philippines Act of 1997" "The Authority shall be the catalyst for the formulation of a national framework for water resources management based on a decentralized, community-based and participatory approach. The Authority,shall create an environment conducive to increased private sector participation in water resources development. The Authority shall facilitate the preparation, integration, coordination, and supervision of all plans, programs, projects, and activitie
